summary.text: 回 is a whole graph associated with turning or circular motion. Its exact early referent is uncertain; common uses include “return” and counting an occurrence.

formation.text: The graph is best treated as a pictograph of a spiral or revolving form. One interpretation specifies water turning in a circle, but the depicted object and exact original meaning remain uncertain. A competing proposal treats 回 and 囘 as originally distinct graphs and words, with 回 meaning “around”; their relationship is unresolved. No separate semantic or phonetic parts within 回 are established.

components.text: 回 is represented as one whole picture associated with a spiral or circular motion. The traditional description of an outer 囗 and an inner revolving shape is an account of its appearance, not proof that these are independent components.

history.text: Historical accounts describe circular or revolving forms and label examples as oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and clerical script. These labels do not establish a verified sequence of graphic changes.

The traditional account describes an outer 囗 enclosing a shape resembling rotation. A competing proposal treats 囘 and 回 as originally distinct graphs and words, suggesting 回 was made for “around” and modeled on 圍. Their relationship remains unresolved.

In 迴, 回 is reported as a sound-and-meaning component. The two graphs share Mandarin huí and have corresponding historical readings in the cited reconstruction systems; this compound role does not establish a phonetic part in 回’s own origin.

uncertainties.text: The spiral or circular-motion interpretation is supported, but the depicted object and exact earliest meaning remain uncertain. The competing distinction between 囘 and 回 cannot be fully assessed from the available account.

The earliest attested sense and any chronology linking turning, returning, replying, and occurrence-counting have not been established. Dictionary glosses and literary examples do not by themselves show that sequence.
The proposed derivation of the ethnonym 回回 from Uyghur or Old Turkic forms remains unverified; the source word and historical sound match are uncertain.
The sound relationship between 回 and 迴 is supported, but when 迴 arose or when the graphs became variant or distributionally distinct spellings is unresolved.

senses.text: Turning or revolving is proposed as the graph’s early meaning, but no securely dated contextual occurrence establishes it as the earliest attested sense.
“Return” is a common current meaning. Its historical relationship to the turning sense is unresolved.
回 can refer to one time or occurrence and serve as a counter. The evidence does not date this use or show how it developed.

limitations.text: The available examples and glosses do not establish the chronology or semantic pathway connecting turning, returning, and occurrence-counting uses.

The proposed 回回 ethnonym borrowing is a separate account of a word written with this graph, not evidence of a semantic development from 回. The proposed source and sound-based borrowing remain unverified.

overview.text: 回 is a whole, picture-like graph associated with turning or circular motion. Its exact early referent is uncertain. Common uses include “return” and counting an occurrence.

components.text: Read 回 as one whole picture associated with circular motion; its outer and inner shapes are not established as separate meaning-bearing parts.
